assurance: Internal written uniform overlap gate, exact local identities and conditional tree deletion; no arbitrary-input leaf extraction or global orbit classification.

declarations.name: Lemma1. Pure four-move extraction
declarations.scope: Adjacent three-DT pattern with eight distinct labels; both pivot labels are fixed by every other factor. The pure word(-1,-2,-2,-1) gives two exclusive leaves and preserves every branch label.

declarations.name: Corollary2. Exact cyclic recursion down to degree nine
declarations.scope: The cyclic canonical family reduces exactly to its preceding member after each conditional extraction and explicit relabeling; full A_n is retained until degree9.

declarations.name: Lemma3. Evacuating a block of external pivot interactions
declarations.scope: An exact3m-move block braid conjugates external factors by E and the two core factors by their ordered product. Anchor fixing and the stated product-fixed-set test give a complete conditional cleanup and deletion.

declarations.name: Exact limitations of stronger extraction claims
declarations.scope: Full A13 controls disprove dropping either the external-support condition for the four-move extraction or the anchor-fixing condition for the evacuation. The first control is repaired by the new evacuation lemma. A degree9 cyclic core deletes to a proper degree7 group of order168.

declarations.name: Lemma4. The even-overlap code is a Hurwitz invariant
declarations.scope: The binary support span is self-orthogonal and literally Hurwitz invariant when all intersections are even. Its invariance under the generated group forces an odd pair for every full A_n tuple.

declarations.name: Theorem5. Every full-alternating DT tree reaches overlap one
declarations.scope: Arbitrary polynomial DT input with full A_n and N>5 reaches an adjacent overlap-one pair, using the odd-pair lemma, a five-cycle core rotation and unchanged-factor bringing.

declarations.name: Lemma6. An overlap-one pair exchanges its secondary edges
declarations.scope: A literal Q^3 identity exchanges the two secondary edges while retaining the uncolored tree at that stage.
